req.title: Reject limit above cap
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when the limit parameter exceeds the maximum allowed.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states the system must return HTTP 422 when the limit parameter exceeds the maximum allowed value. From the source, the maximum allowed limit is 1000 (le=1000 in the Query definition). Tests must cover: (1) a valid limit within range (positive/EP), (2) a limit exactly at the cap boundary (BVA at 1000), (3) a limit exactly one above the cap (BVA at 1001 — must return 422), (4) a clearly excessive limit (NEG/EP), and (5) the boundary at limit=1 (minimum valid). This covers both sides of the le=1000 constraint, catching mutations that change 1000 to 999 or 1001, or flip the comparison operator.

tests.name: test_limit_within_valid_range_returns_200
actions: Send GET /tasks/?limit=100 to the in-process TestClient
expected: Response body is a JSON array of at most 100 items
trace: R-TASK-007: valid limit (100) is within [1, 1000], so 200 is expected
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_limit_within_valid_range_returns_200():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get("/tasks/?limit=100")
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    assert isinstance(body, list)
    assert len(body) <= 100
    assert len(body) == 20
